summary.text: Denise Mentzer is a Democratic member of the Michigan House of Representatives representing District 61 and is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Denise Mentzer's general-election opponent is Robert Wojtowicz (R).
She worked as the senior buyer for Macomb County before entering the legislature.

paragraphs.text: Denise Mentzer was born in Mount Clemens, Michigan, and earned a high school diploma from L'Anse Creuse High School, an associate degree from Macomb Community College in 1999, and a bachelor's degree from Baker College in 2009.
Her career experience includes working as the senior buyer for Macomb County and as a government administrator.
In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, she said she worked twenty-five years for the county and was elected a Mount Clemens city commissioner in 2013.
Mentzer assumed office in the Michigan House on January 1, 2023; in 2023-2024 she was Majority Vice Chair of the Labor Committee, and in 2025-2026 she is assigned to the House Oversight Committee.
In the 2026 survey, she listed water infrastructure among her key messages and said she sponsored bills on a prescription drug affordability board and on forgiving long-term medical debt.
